Searched three ways: (a) keyword 'coinhive' over the entire feed -> 6 events, all with sa=192.168.247.131; (b) sa=192.168.247.131 to the prior-round known IPs 37.187.167.47/104.20.208.59/104.20.209.59 -> 2 events; (c) sa=192.168.247.131 to Coinhive IP ranges 37.187.*/104.20.*/217.182.* -> the same 6 events, none lacking the coinhive hostname. All three result sets were complete (returned = total).
evidence: The complete Monero-generating set for BSTOLL-L in cisconvmflowdata is exactly the six Coinhive chrome.exe:443 flows. Verified four ways this round: (1) BSTOLL-L maps to a single source IP, 192.168.247.131 (dc(sa)=1, 765 events), so no flows hide under another address; (2) a whole-feed keyword sweep for monero/xmr/stratum/cryptonight/miner/mining/pool returned only 2 events — ad-pool domains pool.adizio.com and pool.admedo.com from 192.168.105.214 via MicrosoftEdgeCP.exe, not BSTOLL-L — so no mining flow lacks the coinhive hostname; (3) the DNS feed shows the complete Coinhive hostname set is coinhive.com, ws001, ws005, ws011, ws014, ws019.coinhive.com, resolving to 104.20.209.59/104.20.208.59/37.187.167.47, all inside the 37.187.*/104.20.*/217.182.* ranges swept in round 1, which returned exactly these 6 flows with no hostname-less extras; (4) the raw records show all six share one chrome.exe process hash with parent explorer.exe under AzureAD\BudStoll — a single mining session. The final SPL output above shows the six flows with first_start=1534772253 and last_end=1534773920, span 1667 s.

text: In Cisco NVM flow logs for BSTOLL-L's Coinhive mining session, the question's requested generating time is the continuous union of the mining flow intervals, so it is measured from the earliest flow start (fss) to the latest flow end (fes), not by summing overlapping flow durations or taking only one flow.
evidence: The six mining flows in time order are coinhive.com 1534772253-1534772377, ws014 1534772254-1534772267, ws001 1534772269-1534772273, ws011 1534772283-1534772285, ws005 1534772286-1534772298, ws019 1534772317-1534773920. Every gap is negative (-123, -108, -94, -91, -60): each of the five later flows begins before the running max end of the prior active flows (1534772377, the coinhive.com flow's end), so the union of the six intervals is the single continuous interval [1534772253, 1534773920] and the endpoint was generating Monero traffic for every second of it — the generating time is the continuous span, 1667 s. Rival reading 1758 (sum of per-flow durations) is ruled out because the negative gaps prove the flows overlap in time: from 1534772317 to 1534772377 both the coinhive.com and ws019 flows were live, and the sum counts those 60 seconds (and every other overlap) twice. Rival reading 1603 (longest single flow, ws019 alone) is ruled out because all six flows are one mining session — one chrome.exe process hash, parent explorer.exe, port 443 — and the session began at 1534772253, 64 seconds before ws019 started; the question asks for the endpoint's total generating time, not one flow's.
rival: Rival 1: sum the six per-flow durations to 1758 seconds. Rival 2: use only the longest single ws019 flow duration of 1603 seconds. This premise must be settled by the time-ordered Cisco NVM flow records showing overlap across the six mining flows.
stamp_reason: The reported output lists the six flow start and end times, their per-flow durations, the negative gaps between consecutive flows, and the derived first_start, last_end, sum_flow_durations, and span_seconds values. That directly supports the claim that the measured duration is the continuous interval across the overlapping Cisco NVM mining flows rather than a simple sum or a single-flow duration.
holds_reason: The strongest rival readings are 1758 seconds from summing all six flow durations and 1603 seconds from using only ws019. The same output rules both out: every gap is negative, so the flows overlap and summing double-counts time, while the ordered starts show the mining session began before ws019 started, so a single-flow reading is too narrow for the endpoint's generating time.
